name: com.sovereigngl/sgl-developers
title: SGL for developers
description: SGL developer docs, API reference and engine plugins, for games, mods and integrations.

tools.name: choose_integration
tools.description: Given a game engine, platform or kind of project (Unity, Godot, GameMaker, Roblox, a Minecraft mod, a web game, a Discord bot, a stream overlay, a Shopify store…), says whether SGL has a ready-made plugin for it and how to use it, or, when there isn’t one, how to build the integration: the calls in order, where to keep tokens and keys, and which SGL plugin’s source to port.

platform.description: The engine, platform or project, in the person’s words, e.g. "Unity 2022", "GameMaker", "Fabric mod for Minecraft 1.21", "Discord bot in Python".

goals.description: Optional: what it should do. sign-in: Sign in with SGL in the game; match: Event lobbies: the player’s called match, ready; results: Results from the game; events: Create and run events from your own tools; registrations: Sign players up from a launcher or bot; webhooks: Hear about changes as they happen; display: Brackets, standings and results on a stream overlay or website. Games default to sign-in, match and results.

tools.name: get_developer_docs
tools.description: A section of SGL’s developer documentation (the API docs and "SGL in your game"): sign-in for games, the player API, lobbies, results, webhooks, scopes, errors and so on. Without a topic, the list of topics.

tools.name: api_reference
tools.description: SGL’s HTTP endpoints with their scope, the player permission they need, what they do, and example request and response bodies: the organization API (API key) and the player API (a game’s sign-in). Search by path or word, or pick a group.

tools.name: code_example
tools.description: Working code from SGL’s own plugins (Unity, Unreal, Godot, C), as their documentation ships it: install, set up and use, including sign-in, the called match, ready and results. "http" gives the plain HTTP calls (curl and Node.js) for platforms without a plugin, and "webhook" a webhook receiver that checks the signature.

tools.name: game_mods
tools.description: The unofficial mods and tools SGL lists on a game’s page (made by other studios and players, not the game’s developer or SGL): what each does, who made it and its link. Useful before building one that may already exist.

game.description: The game’s name or SGL slug, e.g. "Dawn of War" or "tekken-8".
